column3: やすくて おいしい
column5: That restaurant's food is cheap. It is delicious.
column8: やすい (yasui, cheap) becomes やすくて (yasukute) to join it to the next adjective: “cheap and delicious.”

column3: ちいさくて かわいい
column5: My cat is very small. It is cute.
column8: ちいさい (chiisai, small) becomes ちいさくて (chiisakute): “small and cute.”

column3: しずかで つまらない
column5: My town is quiet. It is boring.
column8: しずか is a na-adjective. Add で to join it to another description: “quiet and boring.”

column3: ふるくて おもしろい
column5: This temple is old. It is interesting.
column8: ふるい (furui, old) becomes ふるくて (furukute): “old and interesting.”
